messages:
anya: quick thought — instead of a linear ramp let's try "pulses" (short bursts) to surface regressions faster. proposing 3 pulses: 0.5%, 2%, 10% with ~10m observe windows. minimal warmup per pulse. thoughts?
jordan: pulses sound promising for noisy signals. main q: how do we handle inter-pulse state like KV cache warm vs cold?
liam: we should tie warmup to a short lease held by the pulse owner. owner gets ~2m warmup at pulse start, then lease expires to avoid stale affinity. also split probe vs production traffic so probes don't skew metrics.
priyanka: +1. for fallback contract proposal: router should accept a single "degrade_score" float [0-1] from observer. semantics: >=0.7 -> immediate soft-fallback to safe-model variant; 0.4-0.7 -> throttle traffic by 50% next pulse; <0.4 -> no action. include a human-readable reason string and probe_id.
anya: sounds good. also propose token-bucket fast-switchback limiter to prevent oscillation — allow up to 3 fast-switchbacks per hour per route. emit metrics fallback_reason, switchback_count, probe_latency.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/feature/traffic-pulsing-phase1 by @anya — canary 0.5% -> pulses scheduled @10:05, 10:20, 10:35 UTC.
jordan: ops question — who owns eviction if observer becomes unresponsive? my proposal: fallback-orchestrator owns eviction after a 90s probe timeout and uses 'degrade_score=1' to force fallback.
liam: add hysteresis: once a fallback is triggered, require 2 consecutive healthy pulses to lift, and at least one full warmup period. prevents flip-flop with transient noise.
priyanka: also require config safety: per-tenant max-pulse cap + global circuit budget. defaults: tenant max 10%, global concurrent pulses budget 5. enforce at router admission.
anya: i'll update the RFC with a state-machine sketch (IDLE -> PULSING -> STABILIZE -> ROLLFORWARD/ROLLOUT_BACK). will add a tiny proto for observer->router: {degrade_score, reason, confidence, probe_id, timestamp}. ping @jordan for review when ready.
jordan: lgtm. small nit: use confidence to modulate thresholds (low confidence => require >0.8 to trigger). :thumbsup:
anya: noted, will include confidence-adjusted thresholds and an integration test that simulates spike/noise.
liam: thanks — happy to help with test harness.
priyanka: sounds like a plan. I'll sketch dashboard panels for degrade_score, pulse_health, and switchback_count.
anya: awesome. merging notes into RFC now.
